::: {#rem-best-subset-hard}
#### Sparse regression is NP-hard

Best-subset selection looks for the regression
with the fewest nonzero coefficients that fits the data to a given tolerance.
Its decision version asks:
given a matrix $\mX$, a vector $\vy$, a tolerance $\epsilon$ and an integer $k$,
is there a vector $\vb$ with at most $k$ nonzero entries
and $\|\mX \vb - \vy\|_2 \le \epsilon$?
@natarajan1995sparse showed, by a reduction from an NP-complete problem,
that this decision problem is NP-hard (@def-np-complete).
An algorithm that finds a sparsest $\vb$ would decide it,
by checking whether that $\vb$ has at most $k$ nonzero entries.
If such an algorithm ran in polynomial time,
@thm-np-complete-in-p would put every problem in NP into P,
and since [P is contained in NP](p-and-np.qmd#thm-p-subset-np),
P would equal NP.
That is one reason practical methods use greedy forward selection
or replace the count of nonzero coefficients with a convex penalty, as the lasso does.

:::
